**3. GENERAL MAINTENANCE STANDARDS**

3.1 All maintenance activities must be planned, executed, and documented in accordance with this Policy and any referenced technical standards.

3.2 Maintenance work shall be performed to a standard that ensures the safety of rail operations and the travelling public, and that protects the condition of the asset for its intended service life.

3.3 The condition of track and signals and communications infrastructure shall be monitored through scheduled inspections and condition assessments, with findings recorded in the maintenance management system.

3.4 Maintenance priorities shall be determined based on risk, asset condition, operational requirements, and available resources.

3.5 Maintenance records shall be completed in a timely manner and retained in accordance with the MSTA Records Management Framework.

3.6 Any deviation from an approved maintenance standard or procedure requires documented approval from the relevant Division Manager, with justification and risk assessment attached.

---

**4. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**4.1 MSTA Board**

4.1.1 The MSTA Board is the governing authority for this Policy and is responsible for its approval, periodic review, and any amendments.

4.1.2 The Board delegates the day-to-day implementation of this Policy to the Chief Executive Officer and, through them, to the relevant Division Heads.

**4.2 Track Infrastructure Division**

4.2.1 The Track Infrastructure Division (TID) is responsible for the maintenance of all track infrastructure assets as defined in Section 2.1.

4.2.2 The TID shall develop and maintain the Track Maintenance Standards, which detail the specific technical requirements for track components, tolerances, and inspection frequencies.

4.2.3 The TID shall plan and execute all track maintenance work packages in accordance with the annual Maintenance Plan approved by the Chief Executive Officer.

4.2.4 The TID shall investigate and report on any track-related incidents and implement corrective actions as required.

**4.3 Signals and Communications Division**

4.3.1 The Signals and Communications Division (SCD) is responsible for the maintenance of all signals and communications infrastructure as defined in Section 2.2.

4.3.2 The SCD shall develop and maintain the Signals and Communications Maintenance Standards, which detail the specific technical requirements for signalling systems, level crossing protection, and communications assets.

4.3.3 The SCD shall plan and execute all signals and communications maintenance work packages in accordance with the annual Maintenance Plan.

4.3.4 The SCD shall investigate and report on any signals and communications-related incidents and implement corrective actions as required.

**4.4 Maintenance Coordinator**

4.4.1 The Maintenance Coordinator is the single point of contact for the coordination of all maintenance activities on the MSTA network.

4.4.2 The Maintenance Coordinator shall ensure that all maintenance work packages are appropriately scheduled, resourced, and coordinated to minimise disruption to rail services.

4.4.3 The Maintenance Coordinator shall facilitate communication between the TID, the SCD, and other relevant parties, including train operators and third-party stakeholders.

**4.5 Competent Persons**
**5.2 Work Package Planning and Scheduling**

5.2.1 The Maintenance Coordinator shall prepare a draft Work Package Schedule for each quarter, no later than six weeks before the commencement of that quarter, in consultation with the TID, the SCD, and the depot supervisors.

5.2.2 The draft Work Package Schedule shall identify, for each work package:
(a) the asset or asset group to be maintained;
(b) the nature of the maintenance activity (routine, corrective, or renewal);
(c) the proposed commencement and completion dates;
(d) the depot or workshop responsible for execution;
(e) any track possession or line-block requirements; and
(f) any dependencies on other work packages or on third-party works.

5.2.3 The Maintenance Coordinator shall circulate the draft Work Package Schedule to the Track Maintenance Committee for review at least four weeks before the start of the quarter. The Committee shall consider the schedule in accordance with clause 5.1 and may recommend amendments.

5.2.4 Following Committee review, the Maintenance Coordinator shall finalise the Work Package Schedule and submit it to the Chief Executive Officer for approval. Work may only commence under an approved schedule.

5.2.5 Urgent or emergency work may proceed without prior inclusion in an approved Work Package Schedule, provided that the Maintenance Coordinator is notified as soon as practicable and the work is recorded in the Maintenance Management System. The relevant depot supervisor shall provide a written report to the Track Maintenance Committee at its next meeting.

**5.3 Work Order Generation**

5.3.1 No maintenance activity on the MSTA network shall commence without a valid work order.

5.3.2 A work order shall be generated in the Maintenance Management System by the Maintenance Coordinator, or by an authorised depot supervisor, and shall contain at least the following information:
(a) the work order number;
(b) the asset reference and location;
(c) the scope of work and relevant standards;
(d) the risk assessment reference, where applicable;
(e) the planned start and finish times, including any possession arrangements;
(f) the responsible supervisor and the names of the competent persons assigned;
(g) the resources, plant, and materials required; and
(h) any permit-to-work or other safety documentation required under the Safety Management System.

5.3.3 Work orders for routine maintenance shall be raised no later than ten working days before the planned commencement date. Work orders for corrective maintenance shall be raised as soon as the need is identified and no later than two working days before commencement unless an emergency applies.

5.3.4 A work order may only be closed out by the responsible supervisor after the completion of all works, the return of any possession, and the recording of completion details in the Maintenance Management System.

**5.4 Depot and Workshop Responsibilities**

5.4.1 Northgate Depot shall be responsible for track maintenance activities on the northern and western corridors, including the Northgate to Strathpine and Northgate to Shorncliffe lines. Northgate Depot shall maintain a minimum of two track maintenance gangs available for scheduled works and one gang on call for emergency response outside normal working hours.

5.4.2 Southbank Workshop shall be responsible for the maintenance of specialised track plant and machinery, including tampers, regulators, and rail grinders. The Workshop shall also maintain the inventory of critical spare parts for such plant. Requests for plant support shall be submitted to the Workshop no later than five working days before the planned use.
**6. COMPLIANCE, AUDITING, AND REPORTING**

6.1.1 All maintenance activities carried out under this Policy shall be subject to compliance monitoring by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee. The Subcommittee shall review, on a quarterly basis, a sample of completed work orders, possession plans, and risk assessments to verify that the requirements of Sections 4 and 5 have been met. The sampling methodology shall be documented and approved by the Subcommittee Chair.

6.1.2 The Safety and Compliance Subcommittee shall report its findings to the Operations Review Panel at each scheduled meeting of the Panel. Where a finding identifies a systemic issue, the Subcommittee shall make a recommendation for corrective action, and the Panel shall determine the responsible owner and the timeframe for implementation.

6.1.3 Compliance monitoring shall not replace the day-to-day supervision responsibilities of depot supervisors, who remain accountable for the quality and safety of the work performed by their gangs.

6.2.1 The internal audit program for track maintenance shall be developed annually by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee in consultation with the Operations Review Panel and the Manager, Track Maintenance. The program shall cover the following areas, at a minimum:

(a) the effectiveness of the work order process, including the timeliness of raising and closing out work orders;

(b) the adequacy of asset condition data recorded in the Maintenance Management System;

(c) the implementation of corrective actions arising from previous audits and incident investigations;

(d) the currency of training and competency records for track maintenance personnel;

(e) the management of plant and equipment, including maintenance logs and defect reporting; and

(f) the accuracy of the critical spares inventory held at Southbank Workshop.

6.2.2 Each audit shall be conducted by a person or team independent of the area being audited. Where the use of external auditors is proposed, the proposal shall be submitted to the Operations Review Panel for approval prior to engagement.

6.2.3 The findings of each audit, including any recommendations and agreed corrective actions, shall be recorded in a formal audit report. The report shall be submitted to the Operations Review Panel within twenty working days of the completion of the on-site audit work.

6.2.4 The Manager, Track Maintenance shall maintain a register of audit recommendations and corrective actions. The register shall record the recommendation, the responsible owner, the agreed completion date, and the date of closure. The register shall be reviewed by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee at each quarterly meeting.

6.3.1 The following reports shall be prepared and submitted to the Operations Review Panel:

(a) a monthly report on track maintenance performance, including the number of work orders completed, the number of overdue work orders, and the number of emergency call-outs;

(b) a monthly report on plant availability and utilisation, prepared by Southbank Workshop;

(c) a quarterly report on compliance monitoring outcomes, prepared by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee;

(d) a quarterly report on safety incidents and near misses relating to track maintenance, prepared by the Safety Manager; and

(e) an annual report on the condition of the track asset, including the results of any track geometry measurements and rail defect inspections.

**4. Overview of the Multi-Stage Process**

All applications must proceed through the following stages in order. An application may not skip a stage, and a negative outcome at any stage concludes the process for that application.

The remainder of this procedure describes each stage in detail, including timeframes, responsibilities, and documentation requirements.

**5. Stage 1 – Application**

**5.2 How to Apply**

**8. Documentation and Record Keeping**

**8.1 Application Records**

The Workforce Coordination Team must retain the following records for each application for a period
of seven years from the date of the decision:

- Form OT-EL-01, including any attachments;
- The Authorised Officer's Stage 1 approval or decline;
- The verification checks and their outcomes from Stage 2;
- The Eligibility Decision record from Stage 3;
- Any correspondence between the applicant, the Authorised Officer, the Workforce Coordination
  Team, and the Eligibility Review Board.

Records are stored in the application tracking system. Access to records is restricted to staff
with a legitimate need to view them, in accordance with the Privacy Policy.

**8.2 Version Control**

This procedure is maintained by the Workforce Coordination Team. Changes to the procedure are
approved by the Eligibility Review Board. The current version is version 4. Superseded versions
are archived and are not to be used for processing applications.
**8.3 Retention of Supporting Material**

Where an application relies on documents that are not held within the application tracking
system, such as medical certificates or roster extracts, the Workforce Coordination Team must
take a copy and attach it to the application record. Original documents are returned to the
applicant, unless the document is required for an ongoing review under section 9.

**8.4 Reporting**

The Workforce Coordination Team must provide a monthly summary of Stage 1 approvals and
declines, Stage 2 verification outcomes, and Stage 3 Eligibility Decisions to the Eligibility
Review Board. The summary is provided by the tenth working day of the following month. The
summary does not include applicant names. It reports:

- The number of applications received;
- The number of applications approved at each stage;
- The number of applications declined at each stage;
- The number of applications referred for review under section 9;
- The average time taken from receipt of the application to the Eligibility Decision.

**9. Review of Decisions**

**9.1 Grounds for Review**

An applicant may request a review of an Eligibility Decision where they consider that:

- The application was not assessed in accordance with this procedure; or
- New information is available that was not reasonably available at the time of the original
  application; or
- The decision was based on an error in the verification checks completed at Stage 2.

A request for review must be made in writing to the Workforce Coordination Team within ten
working days of the applicant receiving the notification of the decision. The request must set
out the grounds for review and include any supporting documents.

**9.2 Review Process**

On receipt of a request for review, the Workforce Coordination Team must acknowledge the request
in writing within two working days. The Eligibility Review Board must consider the request at its
next scheduled meeting. The Board may:

- Uphold the original decision;
- Vary the original decision; or
- Set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision.

The Board must provide its decision in writing within five working days of the meeting. The
decision of the Board on review is final.

**10.1 Applicant**

The applicant is responsible for:

- Providing all required attachments and supporting documents;
- Notifying the Workforce Coordination Team of any change in circumstances that may affect the
  application.

**10.2 Authorised Officer**

The Authorised Officer is responsible for:

- Assessing the application at Stage 1 against the criteria in section 5;
- Recording the Stage 1 outcome in the application tracking system;
- Advising the applicant of the outcome in writing;
- Referring the application to the Workforce Coordination Team where Stage 1 is approved.

**10.3 Workforce Coordination Team**

The Workforce Coordination Team is responsible for:

- Receiving and registering applications;
- Completing the verification checks at Stage 2;
- Preparing the application for the Eligibility Review Board;
- Maintaining application records in accordance with section 8;
- Providing reporting to the Eligibility Review Board in accordance with section 8.4.

**10.4 Eligibility Review Board**

The Eligibility Review Board is responsible for:

- Making Eligibility Decisions at Stage 3;
- Approving changes to this procedure;
- Considering requests for review under section 9.
**11. Decision Stage**

**11.1 General**

This section sets out the process for making Eligibility Decisions at Stage 3, the issuing of
those decisions, notification to applicants, and the recording and retention of decision
records. The Eligibility Review Board is responsible for making all Eligibility Decisions under
this procedure.

**11.2 Consideration by the Eligibility Review Board**

The Workforce Coordination Team must present each application that has passed the Stage 2
verification checks to the Eligibility Review Board at the next scheduled Board meeting. The
Workforce Coordination Team must include with the application:

- the completed Form OT-EL-01;
- the Stage 1 assessment record prepared by the Authorised Officer;
- the Stage 2 verification checklist and any supporting verification documents;
- a summary of the applicant's relevant work history for the preceding 12 months;
- any prior Eligibility Decisions relating to the applicant, including decisions on review,
  for the preceding 24 months; and
- a recommendation from the Workforce Coordination Team as to whether the application
  should be approved.

The Eligibility Review Board must consider each application on its merits against the criteria
in sections 5, 6 and 7 of this procedure. The Board may seek further information from the
applicant, the Authorised Officer, or any other person it considers appropriate before making
an Eligibility Decision. Where the Board seeks further information, the Board must notify the
applicant in writing of the information sought and the date by which it must be provided.

**11.3 Making the Eligibility Decision**

The Eligibility Review Board must make an Eligibility Decision in respect of each application
referred to it under section 11.2. The Board may:

- approve the application in full;
- approve the application in part, subject to any conditions the Board considers
  appropriate; or
- refuse the application.

In making an Eligibility Decision, the Board must record:

- the date of the decision;
- the grounds for the decision, including the specific criteria relied upon;
- any conditions attached to an approval; and
- the names of the Board members present.

**11.4 Issuing the Eligibility Decision**

The Workforce Coordination Team must issue the Eligibility Decision in writing to the
applicant within five working days of the Board meeting at which the decision was made. The
written decision must include:

- the outcome of the application;
- the reasons for the decision;
- any conditions attached to an approval;
- the date from which the decision takes effect; and
- advice on the applicant's right to seek a review of the decision under section 9 of this
  procedure, including the time limit for doing so.

Where the Eligibility Review Board approves an application in part or refuses an application,
the written decision must set out the grounds for the decision in sufficient detail to allow
the applicant to understand the basis for the decision.

**11.5 Notification to the Applicant**

Notification of an Eligibility Decision must be given to the applicant by one of the following
methods:

- personal delivery to the applicant, with a signed acknowledgement of receipt;
- email to the applicant's nominated work email address; or
- registered post to the applicant's nominated postal address.

Where notification is given by email, the Workforce Coordination Team must retain a copy of
the email and any delivery or read receipts. Where notification is given by registered post,
the Workforce Coordination Team must retain the postal receipt and, where available, the
tracking record.
**12. Review of Eligibility Decisions**

**12.1 Right to Review**

An applicant may seek a review of an Eligibility Decision made under section 11 of this
procedure where the applicant considers that:

- the decision was based on an error of fact;
- the decision was based on an error of law;
- new information has become available that was not reasonably available to the applicant
  at the time the application was considered; or
- the decision was made in a manner that was procedurally unfair.

**12.2 Application for Review**

An application for review must be made in writing to the Eligibility Review Board within
ten working days of the applicant receiving written notice of the Eligibility Decision.
The application must:

- state the grounds for the review;
- set out the facts and circumstances relied upon;
- attach any supporting documents; and
- be signed and dated by the applicant.

The Eligibility Review Board must acknowledge receipt of an application for review within
three working days of receiving it.

**12.3 Review Process**

A review under this section will be conducted by a Review Panel comprising at least two
members of the Eligibility Review Board who were not involved in making the original
Eligibility Decision.

The Review Panel may:

- confirm the original decision;
- vary the original decision; or
- set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision.

In conducting a review, the Review Panel must have regard to:

- the grounds stated in the application for review;
- the original application and any supporting documents;
- the written Eligibility Decision and the reasons given for it; and
- any new information provided by the applicant.

The Review Panel must make its decision within fifteen working days of receiving the
application for review, unless the applicant agrees in writing to a longer period.

**12.4 Notification of Review Outcome**

The Workforce Coordination Team must give written notice of the outcome of a review to
the applicant within five working days of the Review Panel making its decision. The notice
must include:

- the outcome of the review;
- the reasons for the outcome;
- any conditions attached to a varied or substituted decision;
- the date from which the decision takes effect; and
- advice on the applicant's right to seek a further review under section 12.5.

**12.5 Further Review**

Where a Review Panel sets aside an original Eligibility Decision and substitutes a new
decision, the applicant may apply for a further review of that substituted decision only
where the applicant can demonstrate that significant new information has become available
that was not and could not reasonably have been made available during the earlier review.

An application for a further review must be made in writing to the Eligibility Review
Board within ten working days of the applicant receiving notice of the substituted
decision.

**13. Record Keeping and Reporting**

**13.1 Records**

The Workforce Coordination Team must keep a register of all applications for overtime
eligibility, including:

- the applicant's name and employee identification number;
- the date the application was received;
- the outcome of the application;
- the date of the Eligibility Decision; and
- the date any review was completed and its outcome.

Records relating to an application must be retained for a period of seven years after the
date of the final decision in respect of that application.

3. Eligibility Criteria

3.1 General Eligibility

All employees are eligible to apply for special leave under this directive provided they meet the following conditions:
- The employee has completed their probationary period (normally six months of continuous service)
- The employee has no outstanding disciplinary action related to attendance or leave misuse
- The leave request is submitted in accordance with Section 5 of this directive

3.2 Casual Employees

Casual employees are eligible for special leave under the following limited circumstances:
- Bereavement leave (up to two days per occasion)
- Emergency response leave (up to two days per occasion)
- Cultural or ceremonial leave (up to one day per occasion)

Casual employees are not eligible for special leave for other purposes.

3.3 Fixed-Term Employees

Fixed-term employees are eligible for special leave provided their contract extends beyond the requested leave period. If the leave period extends beyond the contract end date, the leave must be approved by the relevant Director prior to submission.

3.4 Exclusions

Special leave will not be granted for:
- Routine medical appointments (covered under personal/carers leave)
- School events or childcare arrangements (covered under personal/carers leave)
- Travel or holiday purposes
- Personal business that can reasonably be conducted outside working hours

Employees should note that submission of a Special Leave Application Form does not constitute approval. Leave is not approved until the applicant receives written confirmation from the relevant approval authority. Employees who commence leave before receiving written confirmation do so at their own risk.

5.8 Withdrawal of Application

An employee may withdraw a special leave application at any time before a decision is made. Withdrawal must be notified in writing to the HR Liaison or, for applications within a supervisor's approval authority, to the supervisor. A withdrawn application will be recorded as withdrawn in the HR leave management system and will not be counted toward any leave entitlement.

6. Assessment Criteria

6.1 General Principles

The following principles apply to the assessment of all special leave applications:

- The circumstances of each application will be considered on its merits
- Leave will not be unreasonably refused
- The operational requirements of the employee's work area will be taken into account
- The employee's shift preference, where recorded, will be considered
- The employee's leave history and any previous special leave applications will be reviewed

6.2 Operational Requirements

Approval of special leave is subject to the operational requirements of the employee's work area. Supervisors and managers must consider the impact of the proposed leave on:

- Staffing levels and roster coverage
- Safety critical roles and minimum staffing requirements
- Scheduled maintenance activities and project deadlines
- The availability of suitably qualified relief staff

Where a supervisor or manager considers that the proposed leave would compromise operational requirements, they must provide a written explanation to the applicant and the HR Liaison.
6.3 Leave Types Covered

The following types of special leave may be approved under this Directive:

- **Personal Leave**: Where an employee is unable to attend work due to a personal illness, injury, or an unexpected personal circumstance that requires the employee's immediate attention. This does not include planned medical appointments, which should be arranged outside rostered hours where practicable or taken as ordinary personal/carer's leave.
- **Carer's Leave**: Where an employee needs to provide care or support to a member of their immediate family or household who is ill, injured, or experiencing an unexpected emergency. This includes care for a dependent child whose usual care arrangement has unexpectedly broken down.
- **Emergency Leave**: Where an employee is unable to attend work due to an emergency affecting their home, property, or family, such as storm damage, flooding, a house fire, or a serious accident involving a family member. Emergency leave may also be approved where an employee is required to remain at home due to a declared local emergency or public health direction.
- **Compassionate Leave**: Where an employee needs time off due to the death or serious illness of a close family member or a member of the employee's household. Compassionate leave is generally limited to two consecutive working days per occasion, unless the circumstances require a longer absence.
- **Community Service Leave**: Where an employee is required to attend jury service, act as a witness in court proceedings, or perform voluntary emergency management duties (such as attendance as a volunteer firefighter or SES member during a declared incident). Employees must provide evidence of the requirement to attend.

6.4 Conditions for Approval

Approval of special leave is subject to the following conditions:

- The employee must have exhausted, or be unable to reasonably access, other applicable leave entitlements (such as personal/carer's leave) for the same purpose, unless the circumstances are of an urgent or emergency nature.
- The leave must not exceed five consecutive working days, unless an exception is approved by the HR Department on the recommendation of the relevant General Manager.
- The employee must notify their supervisor as soon as practicable, and in any event before the start of the rostered shift where possible. Where notification cannot be given in advance, the employee must contact the supervisor by telephone or other available means at the earliest opportunity.
- The employee must complete and submit a Special Leave Application Form within two working days of returning to work, unless an extension has been granted by the HR Liaison.
- Approval may be withdrawn where the employee fails to provide reasonable supporting documentation within the required timeframe, or where the stated reason for leave is found to be inaccurate.

6.5 Limits on Special Leave

Special leave is not an entitlement and is not cumulative. The following limits apply:

- A maximum of ten working days of special leave may be approved in any twelve-month period, calculated on a rolling basis from the first day of the first approved special leave.
- No more than five consecutive working days of special leave may be approved for a single occasion, except as provided under clause 6.4.
- Special leave may not be used to extend a period of annual leave or long service leave, except where the extension is due to a genuine emergency that arises during the leave period.
- Special leave may not be used to cover attendance at union meetings, sporting events, or social functions, except where the employee is required to attend in an official capacity as a representative of the employer.
- Where an employee has already been approved for special leave in the current twelve-month period, the approval authority must review the employee's leave history before approving further special leave.
**Special Leave Directive 2024**

**Issued by:** Human Resources Department
**Effective Date:** 15 March 2024
**Version:** 1.3 (supersedes Version 1.2 dated 1 October 2024)
**Audience:** All employees of the Railway Infrastructure Maintenance Division and all associated depots, workshops, and administrative offices

---

**7. Record-Keeping and Reporting**

7.1 The HR Department must maintain a central register of all special leave applications and approvals. The register must record, for each occasion of leave:

- the employee's name and payroll number;
- the date(s) of leave approved;
- the reason for the leave, as stated on the application form;
- the approval authority and the date of approval;
- any supporting documentation received; and
- the number of special leave days used against the twelve-month rolling limit.

7.2 The register must be updated within three working days of an approval being granted or withdrawn.

7.3 Supervisors must retain a copy of each Special Leave Application Form for their area for a period of not less than twelve months from the date of the employee's return to work.

7.4 On a monthly basis, the HR Department will provide each General Manager with a summary of special leave taken within their area of responsibility. The summary must identify any employee who has reached or is approaching the ten-working-day limit, and any instance where an exception to the five-consecutive-day limit has been approved.

7.5 The HR Department must report to the Executive Committee on a quarterly basis. The report must include:

- the total number of special leave applications received and approved;
- the number of applications refused, and the primary reason for refusal;
- the number of occasions on which the five-consecutive-day limit was exceeded by exception; and
- any observed patterns of usage that may indicate a systemic issue, such as a recurring need for special leave within a particular depot or work group.

7.6 Where an employee's special leave usage in any twelve-month period exceeds eight working days, the HR Department must review the employee's leave history and, where appropriate, discuss the matter with the employee's supervisor to determine whether any workplace adjustments or other support measures are required.

---

**8. Review of This Directive**

8.1 This Directive is subject to annual review by the HR Department. The review will consider:

- the effectiveness of the approval and notification procedures;
- any feedback received from supervisors, General Managers, or employees;
- changes to relevant legislation or industrial instruments; and
- any recommendations arising from the quarterly reports referred to in clause 7.5.

8.2 The annual review will be completed by 30 November each year. Any amendments arising from the review will be published as a revised version of this Directive and will take effect from 1 January of the following year, unless the amendment is required to address an urgent operational or compliance matter.

8.3 Employees and supervisors may submit feedback on the operation of this Directive at any time by contacting the HR Department at the address or telephone number set out in clause 9.

---

**9. Contact and Enquiries**

9.1 All enquiries concerning this Directive, including requests for an exception under clause 6.4, should be directed to:

- At 14:38 hrs, Mr. Kostas contacted the Northern Region Train Control Centre via UHF radio and reported the incident. Train Control confirmed that train 4MB2 had passed through the section at 14:35 hrs without any reported issues.
- At 14:40 hrs, the worksite was declared safe, and all work was suspended for the day. The crew was withdrawn to the Wallan depot.
- At 14:45 hrs, Mr. Kostas notified the on-call Safety Officer, Mr. T. Nguyen, by mobile phone. Mr. Nguyen arrived at the Wallan depot at 15:20 hrs and conducted initial interviews with all five crew members.
- Mr. O’Connor was transported to the Northern Hospital in Epping at 15:35 hrs for assessment of his ankle injury. He was discharged at 17:10 hrs with a diagnosis of a mild sprain and a medical certificate for two days of restricted duties.
- At 16:05 hrs, a formal notification was sent to the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee via the incident reporting portal, in accordance with the Incident Management Procedure (IMP-2024-04). The notification included a preliminary severity assessment of **high**, based on the potential for multiple fatalities had the crew not cleared the track in time.

---

**4. NOTIFICATION TO SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE SUBCOMMITTEE**

The Safety and Compliance Subcommittee was formally notified of this incident on 22 July 2024 at 16:05 hrs. The initial notification provided the following information:

- Incident type: Near miss – track worker struck by passing train
- Location: Km 87.4 Up Main Line, between Wallan and Kilmore East
- Date and time: 22 July 2024, 14:35 hrs
- Injuries: One minor injury (ankle sprain)
- Severity classification: **High** (preliminary)

A full written report was submitted to the Subcommittee on 23 July 2024, and the incident was formally classified as severity high at the Subcommittee’s meeting of 25 July 2024. The classification was based on the following factors:

- The close proximity of the train to the crew (estimated at less than 2 metres from the nearest crew member).
- The high speed of the train (estimated at 115 km/h).
- The failure of the protection system to provide adequate warning time.
- The potential for multiple fatalities had the crew not responded to the verbal warning.

Incident Report IR-2024-118 was classified as severity high. Record status: historical. This classification is recorded as historical and final, and is not subject to revision.

---

**5. IMMEDIATE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

Pending a full investigation, the following interim measures were implemented on 23 July 2024:

1. All track maintenance work in the Northern Region was suspended for 24 hours, pending a safety stand-down and review of protection procedures.
2. A mandatory briefing on the incident was delivered to all track maintenance crews in the Northern Region on 23 July 2024.
3. The lookout protocol for worksites adjacent to high-speed sections (where line speed exceeds 100 km/h) was amended to require an additional lookout positioned 500 metres from the worksite, in addition to the standard lookout.
4. A review of the TOA surrender process for worksites on the Up Main Line was commenced, with particular attention to the time required to clear the corridor after the surrender notice is given.

---

**6. ATTACHMENTS**

- Attachment A: Witness statements (5)
- Attachment B: TOA No. 2024/0718-22
- Attachment C: Train 4MB2 movement log
- Attachment D: Medical report for Mr. D. O’Connor
- Attachment E: Site plan and photographs
**7. INVESTIGATION FINDINGS**

The investigation was conducted jointly by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee, the Track Infrastructure Division, and the Signals and Communications Division. The investigation team reviewed the witness statements, the TOA surrender process, the train movement log, and the site plan. The following findings are recorded.

**7.1 Sequence of Events**

The worksite at Km 87.4 Up Main Line was established on the morning of 22 July 2024 under TOA No. 2024/0718-22. The TOA was issued to the track maintenance crew at 08:15 hrs. The crew consisted of six persons:

- Mr. D. O'Connor (track maintainer, injured)
- Mr. P. Singh (track maintainer)
- Ms. L. Tran (track maintainer)
- Mr. R. Kowalski (track maintainer)
- Mr. J. Smith (lookout)
- Mr. A. Patel (protection officer)

The worksite was located on the Up Main Line, which carries trains in the up direction (towards Melbourne). The line speed at this location is 115 km/h. The worksite was approximately 500 metres in length, extending from Km 87.2 to Km 87.7.

At 14:20 hrs, the protection officer, Mr. Patel, initiated the TOA surrender process. This process requires the protection officer to contact the signaller and advise that the worksite is clear and that the TOA can be surrendered. The signaller then records the surrender and the line is returned to normal operation.

According to the train movement log (Attachment C), Train 4MB2, a freight service, departed Wallan at 14:25 hrs. The train was travelling at approximately 115 km/h when it passed the worksite at 14:35 hrs.

The lookout, Mr. Smith, stated in his witness statement that he observed Train 4MB2 approaching the worksite at a distance of approximately 800 metres. Mr. Smith gave a verbal warning to the crew at 14:34 hrs. The crew responded to the warning and moved clear of the track. Mr. O'Connor, who was at the rear of the worksite, slipped on ballast while moving clear and sustained an ankle sprain.

**7.2 TOA Surrender Process Review**

The investigation found that the TOA surrender process was initiated at 14:20 hrs, but the signaller did not confirm the surrender until 14:32 hrs. This represents a delay of 12 minutes between the initial call and the confirmation. The reason for the delay was that the signaller was managing conflicting movements on the adjacent Down Main Line and did not immediately process the surrender request.

The investigation determined that the crew believed the TOA had been surrendered at 14:20 hrs, based on the protection officer's advice that he had contacted the signaller. However, the signaller did not formally surrender the TOA until 14:32 hrs. During this 12-minute period, the crew continued to work on the track, believing that they were protected.

The protection officer, Mr. Patel, stated that he was not aware that the surrender had not been confirmed. He had assumed that the signaller's acknowledgement of his call constituted confirmation of the surrender. The signaller stated that he had advised Mr. Patel that the surrender would be processed shortly, but that this advice was not recorded in the TOA log.

The TOA surrender process requires the protection officer to obtain a formal confirmation from the signaller before advising the crew that the TOA has been surrendered. In this case, Mr. Patel did not obtain this confirmation. The investigation found that this was a breach of the TOA surrender process, as set out in the Northern Region Track Maintenance Manual, Section 4.3.

**3. GENERAL MAINTENANCE STANDARDS**

3.1 All maintenance activities must be planned, executed, and documented in accordance with this Policy and any referenced technical standards.

3.2 Maintenance work shall be performed to a standard that ensures the safety of rail operations and the travelling public, and that protects the condition of the asset for its intended service life.

3.3 The condition of track and signals and communications infrastructure shall be monitored through scheduled inspections and condition assessments, with findings recorded in the maintenance management system.

3.4 Maintenance priorities shall be determined based on risk, asset condition, operational requirements, and available resources.

3.5 Maintenance records shall be completed in a timely manner and retained in accordance with the MSTA Records Management Framework.

3.6 Any deviation from an approved maintenance standard or procedure requires documented approval from the relevant Division Manager, with justification and risk assessment attached.

---

**4.1 MSTA Board**

4.1.1 The MSTA Board is the governing authority for this Policy and is responsible for its approval, periodic review, and any amendments.

4.1.2 The Board delegates the day-to-day implementation of this Policy to the Chief Executive Officer and, through them, to the relevant Division Heads.

**4. Overview of the Multi-Stage Process**

All applications must proceed through the following stages in order. An application may not skip a stage, and a negative outcome at any stage concludes the process for that application.

The remainder of this procedure describes each stage in detail, including timeframes, responsibilities, and documentation requirements.

**5. Stage 1 – Application**

**5.2 How to Apply**

**7.1 Purpose**

Stage 3 is the final stage of the process. The Eligibility Review Board determines whether the
applicant meets the eligibility criteria set out in the Enterprise Agreement and in this procedure.
The Board's decision is final and is recorded as a formal Eligibility Decision.

**7.2 Eligibility Criteria**

The Eligibility Review Board applies the following criteria when determining an application:

- The proposed overtime or special leave is consistent with the operational requirements of the
  applicant's work location, as documented in the roster and work plan;
- The applicant has not exceeded the maximum number of overtime hours permitted in a single pay
  period under the Enterprise Agreement;
- The applicant's fatigue management status is current and clear, with no restrictions recorded in
  the FRMS;
- For special leave, the reason for the request falls within the categories listed in the
  Enterprise Agreement, and the supporting documentation is genuine and current;
- The applicant has not been found to have made a false or misleading statement in a previous
  application within the last twelve months.

The Board may request additional information from the applicant, the Authorised Officer, or the
Workforce Coordination Team before making its decision. Any such request must be made in writing
and must specify the information required and the timeframe for providing it.

**7.3 Decision Recording**

Every application considered by the Eligibility Review Board is recorded as an Eligibility Decision.
Each decision record includes:

- The application reference number;
- The applicant's name and payroll number;
- The date of the decision;
- The outcome (eligible or not eligible);
- The reasons for the decision, including any conditions attached to an eligible outcome;
- The name of the Board member who chaired the decision.

**7.4 Notification**

The applicant and the Authorised Officer are notified of the Board's decision in writing within
three working days of the decision being recorded. The notification must include the decision
outcome, the reasons for the decision, and, where the application was declined, information about
the review process in section 9.

**8. Documentation and Record Keeping**

**8.1 Application Records**

The Workforce Coordination Team must retain the following records for each application for a period
of seven years from the date of the decision:

- Form OT-EL-01, including any attachments;
- The Authorised Officer's Stage 1 approval or decline;
- The verification checks and their outcomes from Stage 2;
- The Eligibility Decision record from Stage 3;
- Any correspondence between the applicant, the Authorised Officer, the Workforce Coordination
  Team, and the Eligibility Review Board.

Records are stored in the application tracking system. Access to records is restricted to staff
with a legitimate need to view them, in accordance with the Privacy Policy.

**8.2 Version Control**

This procedure is maintained by the Workforce Coordination Team. Changes to the procedure are
approved by the Eligibility Review Board. The current version is version 4. Superseded versions
are archived and are not to be used for processing applications.

**8.3 Retention of Supporting Material**

Where an application relies on documents that are not held within the application tracking
system, such as medical certificates or roster extracts, the Workforce Coordination Team must
take a copy and attach it to the application record. Original documents are returned to the
applicant, unless the document is required for an ongoing review under section 9.

**8.4 Reporting**

The Workforce Coordination Team must provide a monthly summary of Stage 1 approvals and
declines, Stage 2 verification outcomes, and Stage 3 Eligibility Decisions to the Eligibility
Review Board. The summary is provided by the tenth working day of the following month. The
summary does not include applicant names. It reports:

- The number of applications received;
- The number of applications approved at each stage;
- The number of applications declined at each stage;
- The number of applications referred for review under section 9;
- The average time taken from receipt of the application to the Eligibility Decision.

**9. Review of Decisions**

**9.1 Grounds for Review**

An applicant may request a review of an Eligibility Decision where they consider that:

- The application was not assessed in accordance with this procedure; or
- New information is available that was not reasonably available at the time of the original
  application; or
- The decision was based on an error in the verification checks completed at Stage 2.

A request for review must be made in writing to the Workforce Coordination Team within ten
working days of the applicant receiving the notification of the decision. The request must set
out the grounds for review and include any supporting documents.

**9.2 Review Process**

On receipt of a request for review, the Workforce Coordination Team must acknowledge the request
in writing within two working days. The Eligibility Review Board must consider the request at its
next scheduled meeting. The Board may:

- Uphold the original decision;
- Vary the original decision; or
- Set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision.

The Board must provide its decision in writing within five working days of the meeting. The
decision of the Board on review is final.

**10. Roles and Responsibilities**

**10.1 Applicant**

The applicant is responsible for:

- Completing Form OT-EL-01 accurately and honestly;
- Providing all required attachments and supporting documents;
- Notifying the Workforce Coordination Team of any change in circumstances that may affect the
  application.

**10.2 Authorised Officer**

The Authorised Officer is responsible for:

- Assessing the application at Stage 1 against the criteria in section 5;
- Recording the Stage 1 outcome in the application tracking system;
- Advising the applicant of the outcome in writing;
- Referring the application to the Workforce Coordination Team where Stage 1 is approved.

**10.3 Workforce Coordination Team**

The Workforce Coordination Team is responsible for:

- Receiving and registering applications;
- Completing the verification checks at Stage 2;
- Preparing the application for the Eligibility Review Board;
- Maintaining application records in accordance with section 8;
- Providing reporting to the Eligibility Review Board in accordance with section 8.4.

**10.4 Eligibility Review Board**

The Eligibility Review Board is responsible for:

- Making Eligibility Decisions at Stage 3;
- Approving changes to this procedure;
- Considering requests for review under section 9.

**11. Decision Stage**

**11.1 General**

This section sets out the process for making Eligibility Decisions at Stage 3, the issuing of
those decisions, notification to applicants, and the recording and retention of decision
records. The Eligibility Review Board is responsible for making all Eligibility Decisions under
this procedure.

**11.2 Consideration by the Eligibility Review Board**

The Workforce Coordination Team must present each application that has passed the Stage 2
verification checks to the Eligibility Review Board at the next scheduled Board meeting. The
Workforce Coordination Team must include with the application:

- the completed Form OT-EL-01;
- the Stage 1 assessment record prepared by the Authorised Officer;
- the Stage 2 verification checklist and any supporting verification documents;
- a summary of the applicant's relevant work history for the preceding 12 months;
- any prior Eligibility Decisions relating to the applicant, including decisions on review,
  for the preceding 24 months; and
- a recommendation from the Workforce Coordination Team as to whether the application
  should be approved.

The Eligibility Review Board must consider each application on its merits against the criteria
in sections 5, 6 and 7 of this procedure. The Board may seek further information from the
applicant, the Authorised Officer, or any other person it considers appropriate before making
an Eligibility Decision. Where the Board seeks further information, the Board must notify the
applicant in writing of the information sought and the date by which it must be provided.

**11.3 Making the Eligibility Decision**

The Eligibility Review Board must make an Eligibility Decision in respect of each application
referred to it under section 11.2. The Board may:

- approve the application in full;
- approve the application in part, subject to any conditions the Board considers
  appropriate; or
- refuse the application.

In making an Eligibility Decision, the Board must record:

- the date of the decision;
- the grounds for the decision, including the specific criteria relied upon;
- any conditions attached to an approval; and
- the names of the Board members present.

**11.4 Issuing the Eligibility Decision**

The Workforce Coordination Team must issue the Eligibility Decision in writing to the
applicant within five working days of the Board meeting at which the decision was made. The
written decision must include:

- the outcome of the application;
- the reasons for the decision;
- any conditions attached to an approval;
- the date from which the decision takes effect; and
- advice on the applicant's right to seek a review of the decision under section 9 of this
  procedure, including the time limit for doing so.

Where the Eligibility Review Board approves an application in part or refuses an application,
the written decision must set out the grounds for the decision in sufficient detail to allow
the applicant to understand the basis for the decision.

**11.5 Notification to the Applicant**

Notification of an Eligibility Decision must be given to the applicant by one of the following
methods:

- personal delivery to the applicant, with a signed acknowledgement of receipt;
- email to the applicant's nominated work email address; or
- registered post to the applicant's nominated postal address.

Where notification is given by email, the Workforce Coordination Team must retain a copy of
the email and any delivery or read receipts. Where notification is given by registered post,
the Workforce Coordination Team must retain the postal receipt and, where available, the
tracking record.

**12. Review of Eligibility Decisions**

**12.1 Right to Review**

An applicant may seek a review of an Eligibility Decision made under section 11 of this
procedure where the applicant considers that:

- the decision was based on an error of fact;
- the decision was based on an error of law;
- new information has become available that was not reasonably available to the applicant
  at the time the application was considered; or
- the decision was made in a manner that was procedurally unfair.

**12.2 Application for Review**

An application for review must be made in writing to the Eligibility Review Board within
ten working days of the applicant receiving written notice of the Eligibility Decision.
The application must:

- state the grounds for the review;
- set out the facts and circumstances relied upon;
- attach any supporting documents; and
- be signed and dated by the applicant.

The Eligibility Review Board must acknowledge receipt of an application for review within
three working days of receiving it.

**12.3 Review Process**

A review under this section will be conducted by a Review Panel comprising at least two
members of the Eligibility Review Board who were not involved in making the original
Eligibility Decision.

The Review Panel may:

- confirm the original decision;
- vary the original decision; or
- set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision.

In conducting a review, the Review Panel must have regard to:

- the grounds stated in the application for review;
- the original application and any supporting documents;
- the written Eligibility Decision and the reasons given for it; and
- any new information provided by the applicant.

The Review Panel must make its decision within fifteen working days of receiving the
application for review, unless the applicant agrees in writing to a longer period.

**12.4 Notification of Review Outcome**

The Workforce Coordination Team must give written notice of the outcome of a review to
the applicant within five working days of the Review Panel making its decision. The notice
must include:

- the outcome of the review;
- the reasons for the outcome;
- any conditions attached to a varied or substituted decision;
- the date from which the decision takes effect; and
- advice on the applicant's right to seek a further review under section 12.5.

**12.5 Further Review**

Where a Review Panel sets aside an original Eligibility Decision and substitutes a new
decision, the applicant may apply for a further review of that substituted decision only
where the applicant can demonstrate that significant new information has become available
that was not and could not reasonably have been made available during the earlier review.

An application for a further review must be made in writing to the Eligibility Review
Board within ten working days of the applicant receiving notice of the substituted
decision.

**13. Record Keeping and Reporting**

**13.1 Records**

The Workforce Coordination Team must keep a register of all applications for overtime
eligibility, including:

- the applicant's name and employee identification number;
- the date the application was received;
- the outcome of the application;
- the date of the Eligibility Decision; and
- the date any review was completed and its outcome.

Records relating to an application must be retained for a period of seven years after the
date of the final decision in respect of that application.

documents.title: Special Leave Directive 2024
documents.content:
This directive does not apply to leave covered by other specific policies or enterprise agreements, including but not limited to parental leave, study leave, or annual leave.

3. Eligibility Criteria

3.1 General Eligibility

All employees are eligible to apply for special leave under this directive provided they meet the following conditions:
- The employee has completed their probationary period (normally six months of continuous service)
- The employee has no outstanding disciplinary action related to attendance or leave misuse
- The leave request is submitted in accordance with Section 5 of this directive

3.2 Casual Employees

Casual employees are eligible for special leave under the following limited circumstances:
- Bereavement leave (up to two days per occasion)
- Emergency response leave (up to two days per occasion)
- Cultural or ceremonial leave (up to one day per occasion)

Casual employees are not eligible for special leave for other purposes.

3.3 Fixed-Term Employees

Fixed-term employees are eligible for special leave provided their contract extends beyond the requested leave period. If the leave period extends beyond the contract end date, the leave must be approved by the relevant Director prior to submission.

3.4 Exclusions

Special leave will not be granted for:
- Routine medical appointments (covered under personal/carers leave)
- School events or childcare arrangements (covered under personal/carers leave)
- Travel or holiday purposes
- Personal business that can reasonably be conducted outside working hours

4. Leave Entitlements

4.1 Paid Special Leave

The following categories attract paid special leave:
- Bereavement leave: up to three days per occasion
- Cultural or ceremonial leave: up to two days per occasion
- Emergency response leave: up to five days per occasion
- Voluntary emergency management leave: up to ten days per calendar year

4.2 Unpaid Special Leave

Special Leave Directive 2024 issue_date 2024-03-15 date. Record status: historical.

All other categories of special leave are unpaid unless otherwise approved by the HR Department. Unpaid special leave will be granted at the discretion of the HR Department based on the circumstances of the request.

4.3 Maximum Duration

The maximum duration for any single period of special leave is ten working days. Requests exceeding ten working days must be approved by the Chief Executive Officer.

5. Application Process

5.1 Application Form

Employees must submit a completed Special Leave Application Form (Form SL-01) to their supervisor at least five working days before the proposed leave commencement date, unless the circumstances are urgent.

5.2 Urgent Applications

For urgent applications (e.g., bereavement, emergency response), employees must notify their supervisor by phone or email as soon as practicable. The completed form must be submitted within three working days of the leave commencement.

5.3 Supporting Documentation

Supporting documentation may be required, including but not limited to:
- Medical certificates or death notices
- Evidence of emergency service deployment
- Cultural or ceremonial event documentation

The HR Department reserves the right to request additional documentation where necessary.

5.4 Approval Authority

The following authorities apply:
- Supervisors may approve leave up to two days
- Managers may approve leave up to five days
- The HR Department approves all leave exceeding five days

All approvals must be recorded in the HR leave management system.

documents.content:
5.5 Shift Preference Consideration

Where an employee has a recorded shift preference, the HR Department will take this into account when assessing applications for special leave. Shift preferences are recorded in the employee's personnel file and are current as of the date of application. A shift preference of night, for example, will be considered in determining whether the proposed leave period is reasonable and whether alternative arrangements can be made to cover the employee's roster.

James Wilson's shift_preference is night. Record status: current. This preference, as recorded in the HR leave management system, is current and will be considered in any application submitted by Mr Wilson.

Employees who wish to update their shift preference must do so in writing to the HR Liaison at least fourteen days before submitting a special leave application, unless the leave is urgent. The HR Liaison will confirm any change in writing.

5.6 Role of the HR Liaison

The HR Liaison is the single point of contact for all special leave applications that require HR Department approval. The HR Liaison will:

- Acknowledge receipt of applications within two working days
- Review supporting documentation for completeness
- Consult with the applicant's supervisor or manager where necessary
- Advise the applicant of the outcome in writing within five working days of receipt of a complete application
- Record the outcome in the HR leave management system

Where an application is incomplete, the HR Liaison will notify the applicant in writing and specify the additional documentation required. The five-working-day assessment period will recommence from the date the complete application is received.

5.7 Acknowledgement of Receipt

Employees should note that submission of a Special Leave Application Form does not constitute approval. Leave is not approved until the applicant receives written confirmation from the relevant approval authority. Employees who commence leave before receiving written confirmation do so at their own risk.

5.8 Withdrawal of Application

An employee may withdraw a special leave application at any time before a decision is made. Withdrawal must be notified in writing to the HR Liaison or, for applications within a supervisor's approval authority, to the supervisor. A withdrawn application will be recorded as withdrawn in the HR leave management system and will not be counted toward any leave entitlement.

6. Assessment Criteria

6.1 General Principles

The following principles apply to the assessment of all special leave applications:

- The circumstances of each application will be considered on its merits
- Leave will not be unreasonably refused
- The operational requirements of the employee's work area will be taken into account
- The employee's shift preference, where recorded, will be considered
- The employee's leave history and any previous special leave applications will be reviewed

6.2 Operational Requirements

Approval of special leave is subject to the operational requirements of the employee's work area. Supervisors and managers must consider the impact of the proposed leave on:

- Staffing levels and roster coverage
- Safety critical roles and minimum staffing requirements
- Scheduled maintenance activities and project deadlines
- The availability of suitably qualified relief staff

Where a supervisor or manager considers that the proposed leave would compromise operational requirements, they must provide a written explanation to the applicant and the HR Liaison.

documents.title: Special Leave Directive 2024
documents.content:
6.3 Leave Types Covered

The following types of special leave may be approved under this Directive:

- **Personal Leave**: Where an employee is unable to attend work due to a personal illness, injury, or an unexpected personal circumstance that requires the employee's immediate attention. This does not include planned medical appointments, which should be arranged outside rostered hours where practicable or taken as ordinary personal/carer's leave.
- **Carer's Leave**: Where an employee needs to provide care or support to a member of their immediate family or household who is ill, injured, or experiencing an unexpected emergency. This includes care for a dependent child whose usual care arrangement has unexpectedly broken down.
- **Emergency Leave**: Where an employee is unable to attend work due to an emergency affecting their home, property, or family, such as storm damage, flooding, a house fire, or a serious accident involving a family member. Emergency leave may also be approved where an employee is required to remain at home due to a declared local emergency or public health direction.
- **Compassionate Leave**: Where an employee needs time off due to the death or serious illness of a close family member or a member of the employee's household. Compassionate leave is generally limited to two consecutive working days per occasion, unless the circumstances require a longer absence.
- **Community Service Leave**: Where an employee is required to attend jury service, act as a witness in court proceedings, or perform voluntary emergency management duties (such as attendance as a volunteer firefighter or SES member during a declared incident). Employees must provide evidence of the requirement to attend.

6.4 Conditions for Approval

Approval of special leave is subject to the following conditions:

- The employee must have exhausted, or be unable to reasonably access, other applicable leave entitlements (such as personal/carer's leave) for the same purpose, unless the circumstances are of an urgent or emergency nature.
- The leave must not exceed five consecutive working days, unless an exception is approved by the HR Department on the recommendation of the relevant General Manager.
- The employee must notify their supervisor as soon as practicable, and in any event before the start of the rostered shift where possible. Where notification cannot be given in advance, the employee must contact the supervisor by telephone or other available means at the earliest opportunity.
- The employee must complete and submit a Special Leave Application Form within two working days of returning to work, unless an extension has been granted by the HR Liaison.
- Approval may be withdrawn where the employee fails to provide reasonable supporting documentation within the required timeframe, or where the stated reason for leave is found to be inaccurate.

6.5 Limits on Special Leave

Special leave is not an entitlement and is not cumulative. The following limits apply:

- A maximum of ten working days of special leave may be approved in any twelve-month period, calculated on a rolling basis from the first day of the first approved special leave.
- No more than five consecutive working days of special leave may be approved for a single occasion, except as provided under clause 6.4.
- Special leave may not be used to extend a period of annual leave or long service leave, except where the extension is due to a genuine emergency that arises during the leave period.
- Special leave may not be used to cover attendance at union meetings, sporting events, or social functions, except where the employee is required to attend in an official capacity as a representative of the employer.
- Where an employee has already been approved for special leave in the current twelve-month period, the approval authority must review the employee's leave history before approving further special leave.

**Special Leave Directive 2024**

**Issued by:** Human Resources Department
**Effective Date:** 15 March 2024
**Version:** 1.3 (supersedes Version 1.2 dated 1 October 2024)
**Audience:** All employees of the Railway Infrastructure Maintenance Division and all associated depots, workshops, and administrative offices

**7. Record-Keeping and Reporting**

7.1 The HR Department must maintain a central register of all special leave applications and approvals. The register must record, for each occasion of leave:

- the employee's name and payroll number;
- the date(s) of leave approved;
- the reason for the leave, as stated on the application form;
- the approval authority and the date of approval;
- any supporting documentation received; and
- the number of special leave days used against the twelve-month rolling limit.

7.2 The register must be updated within three working days of an approval being granted or withdrawn.

7.3 Supervisors must retain a copy of each Special Leave Application Form for their area for a period of not less than twelve months from the date of the employee's return to work.

7.4 On a monthly basis, the HR Department will provide each General Manager with a summary of special leave taken within their area of responsibility. The summary must identify any employee who has reached or is approaching the ten-working-day limit, and any instance where an exception to the five-consecutive-day limit has been approved.

7.5 The HR Department must report to the Executive Committee on a quarterly basis. The report must include:

- the total number of special leave applications received and approved;
- the number of applications refused, and the primary reason for refusal;
- the number of occasions on which the five-consecutive-day limit was exceeded by exception; and
- any observed patterns of usage that may indicate a systemic issue, such as a recurring need for special leave within a particular depot or work group.

7.6 Where an employee's special leave usage in any twelve-month period exceeds eight working days, the HR Department must review the employee's leave history and, where appropriate, discuss the matter with the employee's supervisor to determine whether any workplace adjustments or other support measures are required.

---

**8. Review of This Directive**

8.1 This Directive is subject to annual review by the HR Department. The review will consider:

- the effectiveness of the approval and notification procedures;
- any feedback received from supervisors, General Managers, or employees;
- changes to relevant legislation or industrial instruments; and
- any recommendations arising from the quarterly reports referred to in clause 7.5.

8.2 The annual review will be completed by 30 November each year. Any amendments arising from the review will be published as a revised version of this Directive and will take effect from 1 January of the following year, unless the amendment is required to address an urgent operational or compliance matter.

8.3 Employees and supervisors may submit feedback on the operation of this Directive at any time by contacting the HR Department at the address or telephone number set out in clause 9.

documents.title: Incident Report IR-2024-118
documents.content:
- At 14:38 hrs, Mr. Kostas contacted the Northern Region Train Control Centre via UHF radio and reported the incident. Train Control confirmed that train 4MB2 had passed through the section at 14:35 hrs without any reported issues.
- At 14:40 hrs, the worksite was declared safe, and all work was suspended for the day. The crew was withdrawn to the Wallan depot.
- At 14:45 hrs, Mr. Kostas notified the on-call Safety Officer, Mr. T. Nguyen, by mobile phone. Mr. Nguyen arrived at the Wallan depot at 15:20 hrs and conducted initial interviews with all five crew members.
- Mr. O’Connor was transported to the Northern Hospital in Epping at 15:35 hrs for assessment of his ankle injury. He was discharged at 17:10 hrs with a diagnosis of a mild sprain and a medical certificate for two days of restricted duties.
- At 16:05 hrs, a formal notification was sent to the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee via the incident reporting portal, in accordance with the Incident Management Procedure (IMP-2024-04). The notification included a preliminary severity assessment of **high**, based on the potential for multiple fatalities had the crew not cleared the track in time.

---

**4. NOTIFICATION TO SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE SUBCOMMITTEE**

The Safety and Compliance Subcommittee was formally notified of this incident on 22 July 2024 at 16:05 hrs. The initial notification provided the following information:

- Incident type: Near miss – track worker struck by passing train
- Location: Km 87.4 Up Main Line, between Wallan and Kilmore East
- Date and time: 22 July 2024, 14:35 hrs
- Injuries: One minor injury (ankle sprain)
- Severity classification: **High** (preliminary)

A full written report was submitted to the Subcommittee on 23 July 2024, and the incident was formally classified as severity high at the Subcommittee’s meeting of 25 July 2024. The classification was based on the following factors:

- The close proximity of the train to the crew (estimated at less than 2 metres from the nearest crew member).
- The high speed of the train (estimated at 115 km/h).
- The failure of the protection system to provide adequate warning time.
- The potential for multiple fatalities had the crew not responded to the verbal warning.

Incident Report IR-2024-118 was classified as severity high. Record status: historical. This classification is recorded as historical and final, and is not subject to revision.

---

**5. IMMEDIATE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

Pending a full investigation, the following interim measures were implemented on 23 July 2024:

1. All track maintenance work in the Northern Region was suspended for 24 hours, pending a safety stand-down and review of protection procedures.
2. A mandatory briefing on the incident was delivered to all track maintenance crews in the Northern Region on 23 July 2024.
3. The lookout protocol for worksites adjacent to high-speed sections (where line speed exceeds 100 km/h) was amended to require an additional lookout positioned 500 metres from the worksite, in addition to the standard lookout.
4. A review of the TOA surrender process for worksites on the Up Main Line was commenced, with particular attention to the time required to clear the corridor after the surrender notice is given.

---

**6. ATTACHMENTS**

- Attachment B: TOA No. 2024/0718-22
- Attachment C: Train 4MB2 movement log
- Attachment D: Medical report for Mr. D. O’Connor
- Attachment E: Site plan and photographs

documents.title: Incident Report IR-2024-118
documents.content:
**7. INVESTIGATION FINDINGS**

The investigation was conducted jointly by the Safety and Compliance Subcommittee, the Track Infrastructure Division, and the Signals and Communications Division. The investigation team reviewed the witness statements, the TOA surrender process, the train movement log, and the site plan. The following findings are recorded.

**7.1 Sequence of Events**

The worksite at Km 87.4 Up Main Line was established on the morning of 22 July 2024 under TOA No. 2024/0718-22. The TOA was issued to the track maintenance crew at 08:15 hrs. The crew consisted of six persons:

- Mr. D. O'Connor (track maintainer, injured)
- Mr. P. Singh (track maintainer)
- Ms. L. Tran (track maintainer)
- Mr. R. Kowalski (track maintainer)
- Mr. J. Smith (lookout)
- Mr. A. Patel (protection officer)

The worksite was located on the Up Main Line, which carries trains in the up direction (towards Melbourne). The line speed at this location is 115 km/h. The worksite was approximately 500 metres in length, extending from Km 87.2 to Km 87.7.

At 14:20 hrs, the protection officer, Mr. Patel, initiated the TOA surrender process. This process requires the protection officer to contact the signaller and advise that the worksite is clear and that the TOA can be surrendered. The signaller then records the surrender and the line is returned to normal operation.

According to the train movement log (Attachment C), Train 4MB2, a freight service, departed Wallan at 14:25 hrs. The train was travelling at approximately 115 km/h when it passed the worksite at 14:35 hrs.

The lookout, Mr. Smith, stated in his witness statement that he observed Train 4MB2 approaching the worksite at a distance of approximately 800 metres. Mr. Smith gave a verbal warning to the crew at 14:34 hrs. The crew responded to the warning and moved clear of the track. Mr. O'Connor, who was at the rear of the worksite, slipped on ballast while moving clear and sustained an ankle sprain.

**7.2 TOA Surrender Process Review**

The investigation found that the TOA surrender process was initiated at 14:20 hrs, but the signaller did not confirm the surrender until 14:32 hrs. This represents a delay of 12 minutes between the initial call and the confirmation. The reason for the delay was that the signaller was managing conflicting movements on the adjacent Down Main Line and did not immediately process the surrender request.

The investigation determined that the crew believed the TOA had been surrendered at 14:20 hrs, based on the protection officer's advice that he had contacted the signaller. However, the signaller did not formally surrender the TOA until 14:32 hrs. During this 12-minute period, the crew continued to work on the track, believing that they were protected.

The protection officer, Mr. Patel, stated that he was not aware that the surrender had not been confirmed. He had assumed that the signaller's acknowledgement of his call constituted confirmation of the surrender. The signaller stated that he had advised Mr. Patel that the surrender would be processed shortly, but that this advice was not recorded in the TOA log.

The TOA surrender process requires the protection officer to obtain a formal confirmation from the signaller before advising the crew that the TOA has been surrendered. In this case, Mr. Patel did not obtain this confirmation. The investigation found that this was a breach of the TOA surrender process, as set out in the Northern Region Track Maintenance Manual, Section 4.3.
